tldr: PlanBench is an extensible benchmark suite based on International Planning Competition domains that evaluates LLMs on planning and reasoning about actions/change, revealing that even state-of-the-art models fall short on many critical planning capabilities.
contributions: PlanBench: an extensible benchmark for evaluating LLM planning capabilities using IPC-style domains

A structured curriculum of 8 test cases covering plan generation, cost-optimal planning, plan verification, reasoning about execution, robustness to goal reformulation, plan reuse, replanning, and plan generalization
An automated assessment framework with domain-independent and domain-dependent components for generating prompts and validating LLM outputs
Initialization with Blocksworld and Logistics domains, providing approximately 26,250 prompts, including obfuscated versions
methods: The framework consists of domain-independent components (a planner, plan validator, and translator) and domain-dependent components (domain model, problem generator, and template-based translator). PDDL-based classical planning problems are generated randomly, translated to natural language prompts using template-based mechanisms, and presented to LLMs in a few-shot setting. LLM outputs are parsed back into structured plans and validated using automated plan verification tools. The benchmark includes 8 task types, with some test cases using obfuscated domain descriptions containing misleading words or random alphanumeric strings to test robustness.
results: LLM performance falls quite short on many critical planning capabilities, including plan generation, even with state-of-the-art models. The paper reports results for Instruct-GPT3 and GPT-4 across the 8 test cases in Blocksworld and Logistics domains. Detailed numerical results were truncated in the provided text.
limitations: The current testbed relies primarily on symbolic models specified using PDDL and structured inputs compatible with such representations. The benchmark is initialized with only two IPC domains (Blocksworld and Logistics), though the authors state they are actively adding more domains. The template-based translation approach may not capture all nuances of natural language planning descriptions.
